## Design Taste
*Source: https://nathanielfaborada.github.io/ — generated by /taste*

Reference concept: a developer portfolio built as a pixel-faithful **Facebook profile clone** — cover photo + circular avatar, Intro/Work/Skills/Education/Social/Collaborators sidebar cards, and projects rendered as feed posts.

### Tokens
- **Colors**: bg `#F0F2F5` · card `#FFFFFF` · border/pill `#E4E6EB` · text-primary `#050505` · text-secondary `#65676B` · heading `#1C1E21` · accent `#1877F2` (the only saturated hue).
- **Typography**: Segoe UI system stack (→ Arial fallback), no web font. Dominant weight 600. Scale: 24px/700 name · 17.6px/700 card title · 15px body (400/600) · 13.12px/600 meta · 12.8px/600 button · 11.52px timestamp.
- **Radius**: 6px buttons/pills · 10px carousel · 12px cards · 50% avatars.
- **Shadows**: `0 2px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.08)` cards · `0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.15)` avatar. Single-layer, pure black, low opacity.
- **Spacing**: 4px base (4/6/8/10/12/16/20/24); section gap fixed 16px; grid gutter 16px.
- **Grid**: 2 columns `360px 842px` (fixed sidebar + feed), ~1218px total.
- **Motion**: `background`/`color` transitions 0.15–0.2s ease-in-out only. No `:focus-visible`, no reduced-motion handling (both are gaps to improve on, not patterns to copy).

### Directives
- When laying out the page, always reuse a recognizable social-profile shell (cover + avatar + sidebar cards + main feed) — because recognition beats comprehension and lets visitors spend attention on the work, not the navigation.
- When presenting a project, always frame it as a feed post (author row + verified check + date badge + "See more" + hashtag tech tags + image carousel + Source/Visit actions) — because a feed invites frictionless scrolling, so more projects get viewed.
- When establishing hierarchy, always drive emphasis with font-weight (600/700) on a compressed 11.5–17.6px scale — because a profile reads as information, not a pitch, and big headings break the "real account" illusion.
- When applying color, always keep `#1877F2` for interactive affordances only (links, primary buttons, active-tab underline) — because a single accent makes "clickable" unambiguous.

### Anti-patterns
- Never load a brand/display webfont (Inter, Clash, serif display) — the mimicry depends on the platform's actual system font; a designed typeface announces "crafted website" and breaks the illusion.
- Never use 40px+ display headings or a tall type scale — it wastes the vertical rhythm the feed needs.
- Never spread the accent across headers, borders, icons, or backgrounds — keep it on affordances only.
- Avoid heavy elevation, borders-as-dividers, or decorative gradients — depth comes from ≤0.15-opacity single-layer shadows lifting cards off the `#F0F2F5` canvas.
- Do not center sections — everything is left-aligned to preserve the "reading a feed" feel.
